fields.narrative_intro: *A lovestruck person and a scatterbrained person discuss GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol at a robot therapist's waiting room.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
LOVESTRUCK PERSON: "GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol—those names have tremendous chemistry."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "I assumed Sol was the office Wi-Fi."
fields.panel2:
[build]
LOVESTRUCK PERSON: "Astra is dazzling; Sol brings warmth."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Or they're a launch, a romance, or my missed appointment."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
LOVESTRUCK PERSON: "The title has no comma: GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Are they partners, or is Astra describing Sol?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The robot therapist silently circles the blank space between “Astra” and “Sol”; both characters stare at it.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
LOVESTRUCK PERSON: "Even the punctuation refuses to define the relationship."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Classic situationship."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A tiny comma occupies the therapist's third chair, holding a clipboard marked “It's complicated.”]

narrative_summary: A lovestruck person turns the title's missing comma into a full romantic crisis in robot therapy.
rationale: Candidate 4 turns the headline’s ambiguity into a specific punctuation-based relationship crisis, then pays it off with the comma as a literal therapy participant. Its escalation is more focused and its “situationship” button lands harder than the other candidates’ variations on simply calling Astra and Sol a couple.
place: at a robot therapist's waiting room
hat_pair: foam clipboard worn as a flat hat with an endless to-do checklist scrolling off the brim
foam server rack worn as a hat with blinking LED lights
